name: Competitor Registry Builder
description: Reads internal links off each competitor homepage and uses Claude to identify the case-results, attorneys, awards and news pages regardless of how they are named, then writes them into the Competitor Registry.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens: 4000, messages: [ { role: "user", content: "You are setting up competitive monitoring for a law firm marketing agency.

Below are the internal links from the homepage of " + $json.competitor_name + ", a law firm competing with our client.

Pick the pages most worth watching every month for competitive change. Firms name these pages inconsistently - case results may live at /results, /verdicts, /settlements, /our-wins or /case-studies; awards may live at /awards, /recognition, /honors or /accomplishments. Judge by what the page IS, not what it is called.

Categories, in priority order:
1. case_results - verdicts, settlements, recoveries
2. attorneys - the attorney roster or team page
3. awards - awards, rankings, recognition, honors
4. news - firm news, press releases, announcements

Pick AT MOST ONE page per category, and only the top-level index page for that category, never an individual case or attorney bio. Skip a category entirely if no link plausibly matches. Prefer shorter URLs over deeper ones.

LINKS:
" + $json.link_list + "

Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no preamble or code fences:
{"pages": [{"url": "https://...", "category": "case_results", "page_label": "case results", "confidence": 0.0}]}

confidence is 0 to 1. Return an empty pages array if nothing clearly matches." } ] }) }}

parameters.content:
## Page discovery, run on demand

Firms name their pages inconsistently. Case results might be /results, /verdicts, /our-wins or /accomplishments. Hardcoding paths misses most of them.

This reads the actual links off each homepage and lets the model judge what each page IS rather than what it is called, then writes the good ones into the registry.

Discovery runs occasionally, not monthly - finding pages is a setup cost, watching them is the recurring one.
